Capabilities.description:
List of task provider capabilities (optional).
If the value returned is null or empty list,
Task Center will fallback to the default value of each individual capability.

Capability.description:
A name=value pair, defining a given capability, supported by the task provider.
The task provider needs to return the capabilities it supports.
Omitting a capability implies the default value will be used (see below).
The following capabilities are supported:
* tasks.pull:
    * Always true - required by the SPI
* taskDefinitions.pull:
    * Always true - required by the SPI
* tasks.push: Should only be provided, if the task provider supports PUSH mechanism for task updates.
    * Default: false.

urn.description:
A globally unique URN-based identifier of an entity in the task domain, consisting of a common prefix and a number of segments:

'urn:sap.odm.bpm.\<entityType\>:\<appId\>:\<appInstId\>:\<tenantId\>:\<localId\>'

The entityType segment is specific for the entity in question and static in nature and must be a lower-case, singular term containing letters only representing the entity itself, e.g. 'task' for tasks, 'taskdefinition' for task definitions, etc. Child entities should override this part of the regex and provide for a fixed string.

All other segments appId, appInstId, tenantId, and localId follow the syntax for valid URI path segments as defined in http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc3986#section-3.3 with the exception of the colon ':' which is reserved to separate the segments from each other.

pchar = unreserved / pct-encoded / sub-delims / "@"

pct-encoded = "%" HEXDIG HEXDIG

unreserved  = ALPHA / DIGIT / "-" / "." / "_" / "~"

sub-delims  = "!" / "$" / "&" / "'" / "(" / ")"
            / "*" / "+" / "," / ";" / "="


So it's basically A–Z, a–z, 0–9, -, ., _, ~, !, $, &, ', (, ), *, +, ,, ;, =, @, as well as % that must be followed by two hexadecimal digits.

Any other character/byte needs to be encoded using percent encoding as defined in http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc3986#section-2.1

status.description:
The status of the task.

* `READY` - Task has been created and is ready to be processed by any recipient; this should be the default starting state for *OPEN* tasks
* `RESERVED` - Task has been exclusively reserved for processing by one recipient who is now also the task's processor
* `IN_PROGRESS` - Task is currently being processed by the processor (*DEPRECATED* and kept for backwards compatibility reasons only)
* `FOR_RESUBMISSION` -  Task has been postponed (and implicitly reserved) by a recipient and will be snoozed for a certain time (at which it returns as reserved for the processor)
* `INACTIVE` - Task has been (temporarily) revoked by the task provider and will disappear from all recipients' inbox
* `COMPLETED` - Task was successfully brought to completion by the processor
* `CANCELED` - Task is no longer available for processing (for whatever reason, e.g. cancellation, deletion [tomb stoning])

TaskDetailsSettings.description: Bundles together web and mobile task detail UI settings

uiType.description:
Type of the task details UI to be used by the web app
  * Default - built-in generic UI, containing task header data, custom attributes and long text description
      * Configurable properties: none
  * BuiltIn - built-in, task type specific, UI (only available for some task types)
      * Using the /details endpoint to request the UI data
      * Configurable properties:
        * enableActions
        * enableAttachments
        * enableComments
        * dataDetailsParameters
  * DataDriven - special built-in UI, expecting a predefined task details data structure, to populate the task details UI
      * Using the /details endpoint to request the UI data
      * Configurable properties:
        * dataDetailsParameters
  * IFrame - the remote UI is loaded via an IFrame or Web View
      * The remote UI URL is part of the Task instance - the first of:
          * mobileUiLink
          * embeddableUiLink
          * uiLink
      * Configurable properties:
        * enableActions
        * enableAttachments
        * enableComments
        * urlParams
  * Form - declarative UI, leveraging the /details endpoint to obtain both the form layout in JSON format and the JSON data to populate it
      * Configurable properties:
        * enableActions
        * enableAttachments
        * enableComments
        * formDetailsParameters
        * dataDetailsParameters
Based on the uiType, only the respective *UISettings fields should be populated, except for Default uiType.

accept.description:
Results in a specific Accept request header.
A comma-separated list of MIME types understood by the client, represented as a standard
HTTP header (see https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc2616#section-14.1). Note that the Accept
header supports parameter passing by appending any number of key/value pairs to the MIME
type:

```
media-range    = ( "*/*"
  | ( type "/" "*" )
  | ( type "/" subtype )
  ) *( ";" parameter )
type = token
subtype = token
parameter = attribute "=" value
attribute = token
value = token | quoted-string
```

* examples
    * Simple - 'application/vnd.sap.concur.travel-expense-details+json'
    * With Parameters - 'application/vnd.sap.concur.travel-expense-details+json;param1=val1;param2=val2'

type.description:
The data type of the custom attribute. Clients MUST follow the ignore rule in
that they MUST be able to silently disregard new data types that are added
in the future. Attribute values are technically always represented as strings,
so when presented with a data type not understood by the client, the client MUST
fall back to an attribute of type STRING and present the actual values as such.

* `STRING` - A string of up to 255 printable characters
* `BOOLEAN` - A boolean value, i.e. either true or false, represented as a string
* `INTEGER` - An integer number in the value range -2147483648 to 2147483647, represented as a string
* `FLOAT` - A double precision floating point number ranging from -1.7976931348623157E308 to 1.7976931348623157E308, represented as a string
* `DATE` - A calendar date following the pattern ^\d{4}-(?:0[1-9]|1[0-2])-(?:0[1-9]|[1-2]\d|3[0-1])$, represented as a string
* `DATETIME` - A timezone-aware timestamp following the pattern ^\d{4}-(?:0[1-9]|1[0-2])-(?:0[1-9]|[1-2]\d|3[0-1])T(?:[0-1]\d|2[0-3]):[0-5]\d:[0-5]\d\.\d{3}Z$, represented as a string
* `TIME` - A time of day following the pattern ^(?:[0-1]\d|2[0-3]):[0-5]\d:[0-5]\d$, represented as a string

format.description:
A modifier property that provides additional instructions to the client on how
to render a custom attribute of a given type. Clients that do not recognize a
specific format MUST default back to the type alone, as if the format was not
specified.

The formats currently defined are:
`type` | `format` | `Comments`
------ | -------- | --------
`STRING` | `CURRENCY` | A currency, expressed as a combination of an [ISO 4217](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_4217) currency code and a decimal number, e.g. "USD 200.99"
`DATETIME` | `DATE` | A timezone-aware date
`STRING` | `DURATION` | Duration of time [https://www.w3.org/TR/xmlschema11-2/#duration](https://www.w3.org/TR/xmlschema11-2/#duration), expressed as defined here [https://www.w3.org/TR/xmlschema11-2/#nt-durationRep](https://www.w3.org/TR/xmlschema11-2/#nt-durationRep). Following the pattern: -?P((([0-9]+Y([0-9]+M)?([0-9]+D)?|([0-9]+M)([0-9]+D)?|([0-9]+D))(T(([0-9]+H)([0-9]+M)?([0-9]+(\\.[0-9]+)?S)?|([0-9]+M)([0-9]+(\\.[0-9]+)?S)?|([0-9]+(\\.[0-9]+)?S)))?)|(T(([0-9]+H)([0-9]+M)?([0-9]+(\\.[0-9]+)?S)?|([0-9]+M)([0-9]+(\\.[0-9]+)?S)?|([0-9]+(\\.[0-9]+)?S))))

name.description: The localized title of the custom attribute

rank.description:
Defines the custom attributes importance and display order.
  * Higher rank means higher importance.
  * Example: custom attributes (CA) with respective ranks: 50, 40, 30, ... 0, would be ordered in the UI like
    * CA1 with rank 50 will be shown first
    * CA2 with rank 40 will be shown second
    * CA3 with rank 30 will be shown third
    * ...
    * CAn with rank 0 will be shown last
    * Custom attributes with the same rank will be shown one after the other, in random order.
  * It is recommended for providers to use 10s or 100s, so new attributes can be inserted, without rearranging the others.

text.description: The actual text localized in the language as per the language code

isDefault.description:
When the default fallback language code is known, set in the respective localized text "isDefault" property to true.

Note
* Only one of the translations can be marked as default.
* Language code '\*' and a default translation are mutually exclusive. 
  If you mark a translation as default with isDefault: true, you should not return an entry with unknown language code ('\*') in the list.

LocalizedText.description: A value type representing a piece of text translated into a number of languages

LanguageCode.description:
A code identifying the language used, consisting of a lowercase, two-letter ISO 639-1 code (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_ISO_639-1_codes), followed by a dash '-'  and a capitalized, two-letter ISO 3166-2 sub-code in capital letters that specifies the national variety (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-2). Examples: en-US, fr-FR, de-DE, de-AT, ...  See https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Language_localisation for additional information.

The '*' language code, stands for a fallback text, which will be used when the translation,  requested by the business user, is not available and the fallback language code is unknown.

code.description:
Technical code of the error to be used for support purposes.

Error codes SHOULD follow dot notation. The code SHOULD start with the applicationId of the task provider the error originated from.

The prefix 'sap.taskcenter.' is reserved for use by SAP Task Center.

details.description: Nested errors required for error processing

400.description: Incorrect request. Format or structure invalid

403.description: Access forbidden. The caller does not have the required permissions to access the resource

404.description: Resource not found. The caller either provided a wrong URL or the requested resource does not exist (any longer).

409.description: Request conflict. State of the resource does not permit the request.

429.description: Too many requests. The caller has sent too many requests in a given amount of time

500.description: Internal server error. The requested operation led to an error during execution

501.description: Not implemented. The server does not support the functionality required to fulfill the request

503.description: Service unavailable. The server is not able to handle the request at present. If no Retry-After is given, the client SHOULD handle the response as it would for a 500 response.

Retry-After.description: Indicates how long the client should wait before making a follow-up request, specified as a number of seconds
